questionText: A person sold two different items at the same price. He made 10% profit in one item, and 10% loss in the other item. In selling these two items, the person made a total of
explanation:
Step 1: Given Information
Let the Selling Price ($SP$) of each item be $S$.
Profit on first item = $10\%$
Loss on second item = $10\%$

Step 2: Calculate Cost Price ($CP$) for each item
Cost Price of first item ($CP_1$):
$CP_1 = \frac{S}{1 + 0.10} = \frac{S}{1.1} = \frac{10S}{11}$

Cost Price of second item ($CP_2$):
$CP_2 = \frac{S}{1 - 0.10} = \frac{S}{0.9} = \frac{10S}{9}$

Step 3: Total Cost Price and Total Selling Price
Total $SP = S + S = 2S$
Total $CP = \frac{10S}{11} + \frac{10S}{9} = 10S \times \left( \frac{9 + 11}{99} \right) = \frac{200S}{99}$

Step 4: Overall Loss Percentage
Since Total $CP >$ Total $SP$, there is an overall loss.
$\text{Loss} = \text{Total } CP - \text{Total } SP = \frac{200S}{99} - 2S = \frac{2S}{99}$

$\text{Loss Percentage} = \left( \frac{\text{Loss}}{\text{Total } CP} \right) \times 100 = \left( \frac{\frac{2S}{99}}{\frac{200S}{99}} \right) \times 100 = 1\%$ loss.

Shortcut Formula:
When two articles are sold at the same price, one at a profit of $x\%$ and the other at a loss of $x\%$, the overall result is always a loss given by:
$\text{Loss } \% = \left(\frac{x}{10}\right)^2 \% = \left(\frac{10}{10}\right)^2 \% = 1\%$ loss.
